adjudicators.reasoning: Spec 5.1.1 says a private clause on an enclosed construct does not cause an implicit reference to the variable in the enclosing construct. Reading B is right that private(t) applies only to the innermost leaf (the loop), but wrong that t is therefore implicitly mapped on target: the target construct has no reference to t of its own, so defaultmap(present: aggregate) does not apply to it. a and b are present from enter data. Program is conforming and race free; the present-mapping abort is a compiler defect (it maps t). Reading A reaches this result.

Reading B fails. It is right that private applies only to the innermost leaf construct that permits it (the worksharing loop). But t is then not referenced as a shared variable by the target construct: the specification states that a private clause on an enclosed construct causes no implicit reference to the variable in the enclosing construct. So t gets no implicit present map on target, and the present failure on a 16-byte object (t) is a compiler defect. a and b are present from enter data. Reading A is right.
